captures.description: THE ARCHIVE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'PennSound is the world's largest free digital archive of poetry audio, featuring over 50,000 recordings spanning from 1913 to the present.' Overview & Mission (CPCW and the Kelly Writers House; the three directors; singles; scope from Williams, Stevens, Stein and Eliot to contemporary poets); Key Features (author pages, 'the Charles Ruas Author Page'; podcasts and PennSound Rewind 'hosted by Michael Hennessey'; PoemTalk with Jacket2; 'open-access and noncommercial'). Twelve cards: CPCW, Jacket2, Wikipedia, YouTube (four), poets.org, Penn Today, X, Instagram, ModPo.

atoms.evidence: PennSound is a poetry website and online archive that hosts free and downloadable recordings of poets reading their own work.
Directors: Co-directed by Al Filreis, Charles Bernstein, and Chris Mustazza.
is the world's largest free digital archive of poetry audio, featuring over 50,000 recordings spanning from 1913 to the present.
Scope: Includes early canonical and modernist voices (such as William Carlos Williams, Wallace Stevens, Gertrude Stein, and T.S. Eliot) alongside contemporary, experimental, and international poets.
Archive Access: All audio files are open-access and noncommercial.
